state.finding: J15 found that test_services_qml_bugs.sh runs its qs probe with the caller's QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland, WAYLAND_DISPLAY and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so in every full suite it connects to the founder's live Wayland display and writes quickshell runtime files under /run/user/1000. The worker contract forbids any GUI process with the live HOME, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or WAYLAND_DISPLAY (a window lands on the founder's screen, a crash toasts the desktop). The lead's scan finds seven tests that start qs directly with no offscreen platform, no own runtime dir and no nested KWin: test_ai_model_picker, test_ai_threads, test_cheatsheet_dispatch, test_lock_pam, test_notification_exec_hint, test_search_commands, test_services_qml_bugs (six unconfirmed beyond the pattern). One of them tests the lock path. An isolated run of test_services_qml_bugs (no WAYLAND_DISPLAY, offscreen, its own runtime dir) is queued to show whether such probes work off the live session.
state.suite_guard: tests/run.sh already clears the caller's XDG dirs and stubs easyeffects for every test (J42). The same place could unset WAYLAND_DISPLAY, DISPLAY and HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE, give each test its own XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and default QT_QPA_PLATFORM to offscreen; tests that start a nested KWin already set their own. A static check like test_private_bus.sh could hold every qs-starting test to it. A test run on its own outside run.sh would still need its own isolation.
